uncertaintyKind: Formal catalog uncertainty; excludes extra shape, spin and thermal-model systematics. It is not the total uncertainty of the displayed physical scale.
additionalSystematics: Usui2011§2.3 explicitly omits unquantified shape/spin/thermal-model effects; rotation can add a few to about10%in size, especially for fewdetections. No invented numerical confidence interval is assigned to these unquantified effects.
diameterSemantics: Mean fitted diameter of a nonrotating sphere in the modified Standard Thermal Model. Its use as the volume-equivalent diameter of the separate convex DAMIT mesh is an explicit display-scale approximation, not a published physical-volume calibration.
limitations: The physical size is approximately calibrated by assigning the AKARI thermal effective diameter to the mesh volume-equivalent diameter. Neither source mesh nor spin is modified. Convex inversion supplies only broad outline; no resolved craters, concavities, reflectance or regolith texture can be inferred. The selected Marciniak (2011) archive model 304 has one pole (266,5) and no calibrated size. Retain it as a convex light-curve model, with explicitly approximate thermal scale and no claim of measured craters or unique absolute rotational phase.
visibleDescription: Convex light-curve reconstruction with approximate thermal size: 64.08 km (catalog ±0.77 km; additional shape and thermal-model uncertainty). Thermal size is used as a volume-scale approximation. The grid marks unavailable imagery.
